s1.syndrome_frame: Hematuria and dysuria with a bladder lesion
salient_findings: Focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
Heterogeneous enhancement of the lesion on CT
key_facts: Past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy
Urinalysis showed 6–8 red blood cells and 4–6 pus cells per high-power field
Ultrasound showed a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall
Lesion demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement on CT
Right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation

shortlist.label: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of bladder cancer, consistent with imaging findings of a polypoidal lesion in the bladder

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of a bladder lesion with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Papillary urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common subtype of bladder cancer, consistent with the polypoidal appearance of the lesion on ultrasound and CT

shortlist.label: Bladder endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a cystic area in the left adnexa

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Rare but possible diagnosis, given the presence of a bladder lesion with calcific specks and the patient's symptoms of hematuria and dysuria

raw.rationale: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder on ultrasound and a well-defined soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall on CT, which demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement, are highly suggestive of a neoplastic process, particularly bladder cancer.

rejected.label: Urinary Tract Infection
rejected.why: While the patient presents with dysuria and hematuria, which can be seen in urinary tract infections, the imaging findings of a discrete lesion with calcific specks and heterogeneous enhancement are more indicative of a neoplastic process than an infectious one.
